current_date: 2019 (the cover reads only 'Local List ... 2019'; the document states no adoption or publication day or month, and cites the South East Lincolnshire Local Plan of March 2019)
current_evidence: The council's Local Validation List page (sholland.gov.uk/article/11295) still links only 'Local List for All Applications (2019)', 'Local List for Householder Applications (2019)' and the Information Checklist, and planning.data.gov.uk lists the same PDF URL as South Holland's local list; no newer SELCP list was found.

issues.detail: Listed building consent is wrong. Grokbot files only Lighting Assessment there, apparently because its trigger names 'a listed building' as one sensitive area near external lighting, which does not make it an LBC requirement. Meanwhile the three requirements the document does apply to LBC are missing from that sheet: Heritage Statement (trigger a. 'For Listed Building Consent'), Design and Access Statement ('All applications for Listed Building Consent') and Structural Survey (listed building works involving demolition or affecting structural integrity).
issues.evidence: Heritage Statement: 'a. For Listed Building Consent;'; DAS: 'All applications for Listed Building Consent.'; Structural Survey: 'b. Any listed building or structure where works are proposed that involve demolition or would affect the structural integrity'

issues.detail: Three Table 1 requirements that apply to full applications are missing from the Full planning sheet. (1) Existing and proposed site sections and finished floor/site levels is filed only under Reserved matters and Householder, although the document names full applications explicitly. (2) Contaminated Land Assessment is filed only under Outline, wrongly noted as 'Application type named in requirement text'. The document names no application type and applies it to all brownfield sites, to land with known or suspected contamination and as standard for majors. (3) Lighting Assessment is filed only under Listed building consent and Householder.
issues.evidence: Levels: 'Required for all full and reserved matters applications'; Contaminated Land: 'The requirement applies to all brownfield sites' / 'should be undertaken as standard for major developments'

issues.detail: Surface Water Drainage Strategy (all major developments) names application types explicitly: a Level 2 Outline Whole Site Drainage Strategy plus a Level 2 Ground Investigation for outline, and a Level 3 Detailed Strategy plus a Level 3 Geotechnical Interpretive Report for reserved matters and full applications. Grokbot has a 'Drainage Strategy / SuDS' row under Full planning only. It has nothing under Outline or Reserved matters, and does not record the Level 2/Level 3 split.
issues.evidence: Surface Water Drainage Strategy: '- Outline applications: Level 2 ...' / '- Reserved Matters and Full applications: Level 3 ...'

issues.detail: The Information Checklist is filed only under Full planning (as INFERRED). The document requires it with all planning applications, and the council page names outline, full, reserved matters and s73/s73a. It is missing from the Outline, Reserved matters and Variation of condition s73 sheets.
issues.evidence: 'An Information Checklist must be completed and submitted with all planning applications.'

issues.detail: Grokbot places almost every Table 1 item under Full planning only, flagged 'INFERRED'. The Outline sheet holds just DAS and Contaminated Land, and the Reserved matters sheet holds just site levels. Table 1 applies by development type, so requirements triggered by major or housing development also apply to outline applications: Affordable Housing Statement (major residential), Planning Obligations/Draft Heads of Terms (all majors), Transport Assessment (80+ dwellings etc.), Flood Risk Assessment, Ecological Assessment and HRA (all housing in the Spalding/Holbeach West SUEs). Conversely, the 'Highways / access details' row under Full planning quotes the Outline section ('the intended access arrangements'), which is an outline-only rule for when access is reserved.
issues.evidence: Outline section: 'Where access is a reserved matter, outline applications must still provide indicative or illustrative details of the intended access arrangements.'

issues.detail: Several other sheets say '(none)' although Table 1 triggers reach them. Variation of condition s73: Agricultural Workers Statement for removal of an agricultural habitation clause, plus the Information Checklist. Demolition in conservation area: Heritage Statement (applications in conservation areas) and Ecological Assessment (applications involving demolition works). Works to trees: the ecological/protected species trigger covers proposed felling or lopping of veteran trees, trees with holes or cavities, or trees with girth over 1m.
issues.evidence: Agricultural Workers Statement: '- The removal of an agricultural habitation clause.'; Ecology: '- Applications involving demolition works to an existing building;' / '- Proposed tree work (felling or lopping)'

issues.detail: Heritage Statement and Lighting Assessment (Householder) share one garbled trigger that merges two table rows and cuts off after 'a.'. Lighting Assessment is not required for all applications. The document limits it to external lighting near sensitive areas.
issues.evidence: Grokbot: 'Heritage Statement Lighting Assessment Required for all applications: a.' vs document: 'Required for applications involving external lighting (such as floodlighting) near sensitive areas'

issues.detail: Six rows carry another requirement's text or 'what is required' content in place of their trigger. (1) Planning Obligations/S106 Heads of Terms uses the Financial Viability trigger ('range of planning obligations required by policy.'); its real trigger is all major developments. (2) Drainage Strategy/SuDS uses a sentence from the FRA content; its real trigger is all major developments. (3) Schedule of works (listed building) under Full planning uses contaminated land remediation text. (4) Archaeological Assessment gives content ('As a minimum...') instead of the trigger: operational development close to designated heritage assets or HER sites. (5) Contaminated Land (Outline) gives content instead of the known/suspected contamination and brownfield trigger. (6) Marketing/vacancy evidence gives a content bullet plus a page header instead of the trigger: loss of B1/B2/B8 employment land.
issues.evidence: Planning Obligations/Draft Heads of Terms: 'Required for all major developments.'; Archaeology: 'operational development is deemed close to designated heritage assets such as Scheduled Ancient Monuments'

issues.detail: Several triggers are cut off at 'a.', so the actual trigger is lost. Heritage Statement (Full) should read: LBC; conservation areas, excluding changes of use with no operational development; material impact on the setting of a listed, locally listed or other designated or non-designated asset. Economic Statement: new major B1/B2/B8 development, or loss of B1/B2/B8 land or buildings to another use. Noise Impact Assessment: new noise-sensitive use near a noise source; new noise-generating use near a sensitive use; or alteration of an existing industrial/commercial site (new plant, layout or working hours). Structural Survey: rural building conversions, and listed building works involving demolition or structural integrity. Other rows carry extraction debris: Roof plan (Householder) has interleaved columns, Tree Survey begins 'accessed at: 0', Transport Assessment begins 'Design Approach': 0' and Affordable Housing begins 'and Surveys'.
issues.evidence: Grokbot: 'Economic Statement Required for applications for: a.'; 'Noise Impact Assessment Required for applications for: a.'; 'Structural Survey Required for any applications that involve: a.'

issues.detail: Ecological Assessment (Full and Householder) is cut to its first bullet, International Sites (SAC/SPA/Ramsar). The trigger also covers: SSSI, NNR, SNCI, RIGS, LNR, LWS and s41 priority habitats; barn conversions; demolition; works affecting roof spaces; floodlighting within 50m of woodland or water; church curtilages; work to veteran or cavity trees; major proposals within 500m of a pond or lake, or minor proposals within 100m; proposals within 20m of rivers; and derelict, allotment or railway land. All of these are dropped, along with the follow-on Protected Species Survey requirement.
issues.evidence: Ecology: '- Major proposals within 500m of a pond or lake or minor proposals within 100m of a pond or lake;'

issues.detail: Thresholds and locations are lost from three triggers. Flood Risk Assessment gives only 'most developments within one of the flood zones'. It drops: flood zone 2/3 including minor development and change of use; sites of 1ha or more in flood zone 1; and sites under 1ha at risk from other sources or with EA-flagged critical drainage problems. Retail row: the text is interleaved with content and drops the sequential test for out-of-centre main town centre uses and the local Retail Impact Assessment threshold of over 250 m2 gross outside Spalding and the District/Local Centres. HRA: drops the second trigger, all major housing within 10km of The Wash and North Norfolk Coast European Marine Site.
issues.evidence: FRA: 'a. In flood zone 2 or 3 (including minor development and change of use); or b. Of 1 hectare (ha) or more in flood zone 1.'; Retail: 'over 250m2 of floorspace (gross figure)'; HRA: 'all major housing proposals within 10km of The Wash'

issues.detail: Five more triggers are partial or come from the wrong place. Floor plans/Elevations quotes the national scale note, not the local trigger (new or altered elevations; new floor space or change of use of floor space). Design and Access Statement stops after the major-applications bullet, dropping conservation area development (1+ dwellings or 100 m2+) and LBC. Landscaping stops at 'normally required ... by planning condition' and drops the cases where it is needed at submission: large-scale development, prominent open countryside, new settlement edge. Ventilation/Extraction interleaves columns and drops the B1/B2 odour and 'substantial ventilation equipment' triggers. Open space starts mid-sentence and drops 'redevelopment or change of use of open space, sporting facilities'.
issues.evidence: Elevations: 'Required for all applications where: - New elevations are proposed; and/or - Existing elevations are altered.'; Landscaping: '- Large scale development is proposed;'

issues.detail: Some Householder rows are keyword matches on fragments, not triggers. Cycle parking details ('vehicle and cycle parking arrangements.') is part of the content of the Parking Arrangements row. Highways/access details ('site including access arrangements;') is a site-layout-plan bullet. HRA ('- International Sites (SAC/SPA/ Ramsar);') is the first bullet of the Ecology trigger, and project-level HRA in the document applies only to housing development.
issues.evidence: Parking Arrangements: 'Details of existing and proposed vehicle and cycle parking arrangements.'; HRA: 'Required for all housing development within the following Sustainable Urban Extensions'

issues.detail: Four Grokbot items are not requirements in the document. 'Travel Plan' (Full) comes from a Transport Assessment sentence saying a Travel Plan is not always required; Table 1 has no Travel Plan row. 'Tall buildings / Wind microclimate assessment' comes from a clause in the Daylight/Sunlight trigger; no wind assessment is required. 'Street scene elevations / Contextual drawings' (Householder) comes from the Heritage Statement photographs item. The tab item '- International Sites (SAC/SPA/ Ramsar);' under 'Policy-driven requirements' is a bare list fragment.
issues.evidence: Transport Assessment text: 'though producing a Travel Plan is not always required.'; Daylight/Sunlight: 'or where tall buildings are proposed.'

issues.detail: The 'Submission rules' tab items are process text from 'The Validation Process' and 'Pre-application Discussions', not requirements: the 3/5 working-day validation check, the 21-day return of invalid applications, the paper-copy note and the pre-application advice expectation. The pre-app note is also turned into a 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' requirement under Householder and Full planning. The Full planning version also has the Table 1 header and the first Elevations row run into it.
issues.evidence: 'If we do not hear from you within 21 days... your submitted application and any associated documents will be returned to you.'

issues.detail: The council web page adds a statutory Biodiversity Net Gain requirement that is not in the 2019 PDF: major applications from 12 Feb 2024 and small sites from 2 Apr 2024. Grokbot does not record it under Full or Outline with that trigger. Its only BNG row is under Householder, and its text is a fragment of the Ecology survey content ('recommendations for biodiversity net gain.'). Householder development is exempt from statutory BNG.
issues.evidence: Council page: BNG required for majors from 12 February 2024 and small sites from 2 April 2024; PDF Ecology content only: 'Make recommendations for biodiversity net gain.'

issues.detail: Some local sub-requirements are not recorded. (1) A full Topographical Survey for major proposals, under the site sections/levels row. (2) A Protected Species Survey where protected or priority species are known or likely. (3) The general rule that technical reports come from suitably qualified people and surveys are no more than 2 years old. (4) The local Site Location Plan rules: scale 1:1250 or 1:2500, two named roads, a red line that links to a highway and includes visibility splays, and a blue line for other owned land. Grokbot has no location plan row.
issues.evidence: 'e. Provide a full Topographical Survey for major proposals'; 'Surveys/assessments should be up-to-date and no more than 2 years old.'; 'the red line must link to a highway. It should also include any visibility splays'

issues.detail: The drawing-standards tab has near-identical duplicates: three variants of 'Be drawn to a recognised metric scale, preferably (at) 1:50 or 1:100', two of 'Include written/annotated external dimensions' and two drawing-number items. Each ends with a stray list numeral ('4.', '5.', 'b.', 'c.').
issues.evidence: Grokbot tab_items, section 'Drawing / document standards'

issues.detail: 'Sunlight to gardens/amenity space' (Householder and Full) repeats the Daylight/Sunlight Assessment row using a fragment of the same trigger ('associated gardens/amenity space.'). 'Photographs / Photomontages' and 'Street scene elevations' (Householder) are both cut from the same Heritage Statement item e.
issues.evidence: Daylight/Sunlight: 'including habitable rooms and associated gardens/amenity space.'; Heritage Statement: 'e. Photographs comprising: a general image showing the building in context'

issues.detail: The list date 2019-09-01 comes from PDF CreationDate metadata. The document itself says only '2019' and gives no adoption or publication date, so the day and month are invented precision. The list is more than 6 years old, well past the 2-year review it sets itself. Its references are also stale (Use Classes A3/A4/A5 and B1, the EIA Regulations 1999, NPPF 2018/2019 paragraphs), and the council has added post-2019 BNG requirements on its web page instead.
issues.evidence: Cover: 'Local List ... 2019'; Introduction: 'The List must be reviewed every two years'

summary: Grokbot's link and 2019 vintage are right, and it captures nearly every Table 1 row of the All Applications list, but the extraction is unreliable in detail. Many triggers are truncated or mixed up with neighbouring rows: S106, drainage, archaeology and contaminated land carry the wrong text, and the FRA, retail, HRA and ecology thresholds are lost. The blanket 'INFERRED' Full-only placement misfiles items: LBC holds only Lighting, and Full planning is missing site levels, contamination and lighting. There are also invented rows (Travel Plan, wind) and process text logged as requirements. The Householder list was not part of the manual upload, so the Householder rows were judged only from Grokbot's own text.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
